title: Merge Two Sorted Arrays

concept.title: Merging with two pointers
body: To merge two sorted arrays, keep one pointer in each. At every step compare the two elements the pointers show, move the smaller one to the output, and advance only that pointer. The output is sorted because the smallest remaining element is always one of the two fronts.
When one array is used up, the rest of the other is already in order and is copied as it is. This merge step is also the heart of merge sort.

statement: You are given two arrays sorted in non-decreasing order. Print them merged into one sorted array.
inputFormat: The first line has `n` and `m`, the lengths of the arrays.
The second line has the `n` numbers of the first array.
The third line has the `m` numbers of the second array.
outputFormat: Print the `n + m` numbers of the merged array on one line.
hints: Keep one pointer per array, both at the start.
Compare the two current elements and take the smaller; move only that pointer.
When one array is finished, append what is left of the other.

starter.python:
n, m = map(int, input().split())
a = list(map(int, input().split()))
b = list(map(int, input().split()))

# Your code here

explanation: Two pointers walk through the arrays. Each step moves the smaller front element to the output, so the output stays sorted.
solution.complexity: Time O(n + m), space O(n + m).

code.python:
n, m = map(int, input().split())
a = list(map(int, input().split()))
b = list(map(int, input().split()))

out = []
i = j = 0
while i < n and j < m:
    if a[i] <= b[j]:
        out.append(a[i])
        i += 1
    else:
        out.append(b[j])
        j += 1
out += a[i:]
out += b[j:]
print(*out)
